August 2010 # Constrained - Refined demand is recovering quicker than expected, leading to a small deficit in Q2 as copper refined production is performing well but not enough to meet immediate consumption requirements. Consumers and merchants face a lack of prompt material, both cathode and scrap, leading to draw downs from exchange stocks and the restricted scrap pool. - The copper market is tight globally, with premiums up across the board. Asian players, who are the hungriest for material, have been very active in South America and are now in the US, after exhausting the freely available stocks in Asia and Europe. - Copper prices broke through the $7,000/t ceiling this week. Higher consumption and the absence of any major negative economic news have encouraged this pickup, and we expect prices to shift up to a $6,600-7350/t trading range through August. |The supply/deman

Forec|ast prod|uction all|ows for p|otential|| © 2010 CRU International Limited **confidential** August 2010 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com # Through the $7,000/t ceiling In late July, copper prices pushed through the top end of the $6,000-7,000/t trading range in which they had been fluctuating since mid-May. This has been the longest period in the past year that copper prices have remained relatively sta

ble. The volatility so far is still within the average levels (on a percentage basis) that have been recorded since 2005. Of late, copper prices have not reacted to macroeconomic events as much as in the first four months of the year. Given that prices did not fall below $6,000/t even when the majority of the macro news was negative, most market participants now believe this level has been established as a firm floor. However, when the next wave of negative macro news comes through we will see if this argument will be validated. In the EU, the combination of bank stress test results and recent evidence of the Eurozone‟s sustained recovery has temporarily eased strains in financial markets. In China, industrial production growth decelerated in June (13.7% y-o-y) well below the average in H1 (17.6% y-o-y) but it is still a robust number. The value of total Chinese exports grew by 43.9% in June, with a surge in capital goods exports. We believe that the rally also included exports of semis brought forward from H2 2010 in advance of the reduction in export tax rebates that were introduced on 15th July. In the USA, the economy has decelerated but recent housing market data – a 23.6% m-o-m increase in new home sales – is the first sign in months that the risk of a serious double dip in housing may be abating. ## **Copper demand recovery beyond expectations…** Refined copper demand is recovering quicker than we expected. While refined copper production has been performing well, it has not fulfilled demand requirements sufficiently leading to a modest deficit in Q2. China continues to lead the growth of the world‟s refined copper consumption and this year it is estimated to account for 38% of the total. Chinese semis production rose 18% in the year to June. Capacity utilisation rates in the Chinese wirerod industry fell from 80% in May to 75.7% in June due to the hot weather (driven by softer construction demand) and the slowdown in winding wire exports to North America and Europe due to the holiday season. However, 80% of the companies surveyed by Antaike indicated that production levels would stay high through August. Demand for semis in Q3 is seasonally the weakest quarter in China. There is also negative sentiment about the government‟s stric

t control on the real estate market and expectations are that demand could see slower growth.  In CRU‟s view, the impact of this policy on refined consumption should not be visible until Q4 at the earliest.  Meanwhile, North East Asia continued to show a y-o-y improvement in demand in the second quarter of 2010.  Japanese refined consumption grew 32.6% y- o-y to 232,000t in Q2, underpinned by robust production of semis production especially in flat rolled products. Semiconductor leadframes and automotive connector pins are driving this strong growth. However, semis output in the region fell marginally on a sequential basis in Q2 after a strong rebound that started in Q4 2009. 

In Western Europe, refined consumption edged up by 3.5% y-o-y in Q2, mainly supported by robust German and Italian semis production.  Nevertheless, countries in Southern Europe are telling a different

Spanish wirerod producers, who rely on orders from the construction sector, have seen no improvements so far and utility companies are understood to be deferring investment projects for the next few years.  In contrast, Finnish semis producer Luvata announced earlier in July that it will consume 15% more copper this year with most of the improvement in demand attributed to Asia and the US.  The US auto sector continues to see y-o-y increases in production volumes while the commercial building sector is still dragging on any hopes of a rapid growth.  This mixed economic data only goes to remind us that the path of recovery will not be easy.  We believe that Brazil will be the main source of momentum in the Americas, with refined copper consumption rising by 8.5% y-o-y in Q2, and will continue to be driven by the government‟s growth acceleration programme.  Most semis manufacturers in the northern hemisphere are currently taking their 3-4 week holiday starting from mid-July, and business activity will likely be sequentially lower in this current quarter. 

## **… so exchange warehouses’ stocks are being run down** 

Copper stocks in exchange warehouses have been on a declining trend throughout July and have hit their lowest levels since November 2009 at about 615,000t at the time of writing.  Unlike in recent months, the decline in exchange warehouse stocks occurred across all exchanges and all regions, led by the falls on the LME.  The largest stock declines have been at Asian LME warehouses, down by 19,800t in July to-date. The second largest decline was at SHFE warehouses, falling by 10,000t to 113,992t.  Given the level of LME cancelled warrants, which amount to over 10% of total stocks in all regions, we expect LME stocks will continue to drawn down for another month at least, despite this being the “slow” demand season.  We understand that most of the material has been moved off the exchanges.  This has either been consumed or has been bought as par

t of some consumer and merchant restocking to replenish a pipeline that has been totally depleted since the economic crisis. 

Inventory in LME warehouses in Asia has halved since January.  In Europe, there are less than 50,000t of refined stocks left in LME warehouses.  Stocks grew by only 36,000t from the low reached in July 2009 and are now at levels not seen since August 2008.  In addition, the fire at Aurubis‟ Hamburg smelter resulted in a loss of 1,300t of refined cathode which was equivalent to 3% of total LME warehouses stocks on the day of the incident.  This highlights the exposure of Europe to shortages and spikes in premiums should there be any significant supply disruptions.  In the USA, combined LME and Comex warehouse stocks have declined by 9,000t so far in July, to 389,000t.  We expect US LME stocks to fall below the 283,400t level recorded at the start of the year by mid-August. 

Asian traders and consumers of refined copper are particularly hungry for metal.  We hear that Japanese traders are struggling to secure enough material to fulfil their refined export commitments, as producers favour their domestic consumers ahead of the traders.  These traders are adding pressure to an Asian market that is already tight for several reasons.  First of all, scrap replacement demand for cathode due to tight scrap availability is boosting the demand for refined metal in Asia.  Add to this the ongoing structural shift in the Chinese semis industry towards more refined intensive products such as high quality refined-only wirerod and flat rolled products.  We also understand that stock in LME Asian warehouses (almost 70,000t compared to a low of just over 1,000t last year) and those in bonded warehouses in Shanghai (over 200,000t) are being tightly held.  Other short term factors that will boost Chinese demand in Q3 will include SHFE/LME arbitrage related buying alongside a wave of smelter shutdowns which will reduce Chinese refined production in Q3. 

## **Q2 supply fails to meet expectations** 

In the past few months, no major unexpected disruptions were reported to have affected production. However, Q2 outturn so far suggests that producers have not met announced targets.  Lower grades at Ernest Henry, zinc high grading (at the expense of copper) at Antamina and ramp up problems at Las Cruces will

This will result in a production loss of about 41,000-82,000t copper-in-concentrates compared to 2009-2010.  Freeport-McMoRan has pushed back mining of high grade ore previously scheduled for 2010 and 2011 to beyond 2014.  As a result, production of copper-in-concentrates in 2010 will be about 60,000t less than previously planned. 

As we mentioned earlier, the copper sc

rap market continues to be tight. We understand that scrap traders that had bought material when copper prices were around $7,000/t have been reluctant to sell their inventories at prices below this level. We have heard that as copper prices rose above $7,000/t some scrap has been released into the market in China. However, we suspect that most material will be held back, as traders hold off in the hope of even higher prices to come. Shanghai discount more

## **Premiums increasing in all regions** The tightness of prompt availability of material in the market is supporting higher cathode premiums. In Europe, premiums remain in the $90-100/t range although not much physical business is being reported due to the summer holidays. In China, premiums have been volatile responding to whether the SHFE/LME arbitrage was open or not. In early July, premiums were in the $130-140/t range, rocketing to $160/t when the arbitrage window opened during the third week of July, only to then fall back to $120/t once the arbitrage closed. Asian traders and consumers (mainly Chinese and Japanese) **0** are hungry for material and that is encouraging them to be **-5** far more active in South America than a year ago. In fact, there has not been much Chilean material tendered this year, in a time when there are no reported disruptions affecting copper production and we would have expected more spare material to become available. As of July 2010, tenders add up to 97,000t compared to 101,600t on the same period a year ago, when several disruptions took place. This year, the lack of spare cathode is a result of producers being sold out and even seeking shipment delays. The latest public tender was held by Antofagasta Minerals in mid-July. The premium was reported to be $115/t which is well above the level reported in their last tender in April and could well set a precedent for future negotiations. In the US, better than expected consumption and high freight costs have contributed to increased premium levels. We understand that premiums in the mid-west and north-east are closer to 6-7¢/lb, compared to 5- 6¢/lb at the beginning of this month. We have also heard that Asian buyers have been approaching players in the US market. ## **Prices likely to test upside in volatile trading** Price volatility in June and July this year has matched the average seen in the same months over

B3.5T has been allocated to high-speed railway construction, according to the National Development and Reform Commission. China‟s investment decision did not happen overnight; the „Mid-to-Long Term Railway Development Plan‟ proposed by the Ministry of Railways (MOR) was approved by the State Council in 2004. The two major highlights of the plan were 1) the construction of dedicated passenger lines and 2) the development of new lines and the expansion of railway capacity in the western region. The western region consists of six provinces, five autonomous regions and Chongqing, in total accounting for more than 70% of the mainland. According to the plan, the total length of railways in operation will reach 100,000km, of which 50% will be electrified, by year 2020. In 2006, the length of the network in operation was 77,000km, of which 82.3% was owned nationally. A 120km high-speed railway line was constructed between Beijing and Tianjin in 2008, and the investment plan was revised and accelerated in the same year when the country launched the stimulus package amidst the financial crisis, of which 40% was allocated to infrastructure development. ## **Latest progress of railway investment** China‟s railway construction investment has increased sharply over the last 7 years from RMB53B in 2003 to RMB600B in 2009, with growth of 77.9% between 2008 and 2009. In 2009, an additional of 5,557km of railway went into operation, 4,128km of line was double-tracked and 8,448km was electrified. According to the MOR, the total length of railways in operation was 86,000km by the end of 2009 (+7.3% y- o-y), of which 41.7% was electrified. At the moment, China has about 6,500km of high-speed track, which is compatible for trains that travel at 200-350km/h. This accounts for 7.6% of the total length of the railway network. The overall high-speed network will include four routes linking the north and the south, four routes Chart Title

Recent reports suggest that China now aims to complete a high-speed network of 20,000km by 2015. ## **The corresponding impact on copper demand** There is no huge difference between copper consumption in normal railway lines and that in high-speed railway lines. Wires and cables used for railway and train construction are classified as rolling stock cables. The major types within this category are communication cables, power/signalling cables and other components such as winding wires and strips that wind around traction motors and transformers. An industry source says that each high-speed train would require 10t of copper component

s and an additional 10t of copper in the power and communication cables per km of track. Moreover, pantographs (a device on the roof of electric trains and locomotives that picks up the electric current from overhead wires) and track cables are installed beside the track or above the train for electrification purposes. At present, the most commonly used overhead conductor for high-speed railway lines is copper alloy wire which contains over 90% copper. Other elements such as tin, magnesium and silver are added for © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 Copper Monitor August 2010 www.crumonitor.com strength. Major local producers that are producing the bare copper alloy wire for high-speed trains include Yunnan Copper and Chalco Luoyang Copper. The latter says annual demand for this type of cable from high-speed railway projects is 6,000t. We also underdstand that Spanish rod producer La Farga has opened, with two local partners, a new plant called Ganzhou Jiangwu - La Farga High Speed Railway Copper Materials that will produce copper and alloy products for the railway sector. We estimate that the high-speed railway projects will account for more than 50,000t of refined copper consumption in 2010. on 3<sup>rd</sup> July at its **Zijinshan** gold-copper mine in Shanghang, Fujian province, trading of **Zijin Mining Group** ‟s shares was suspended in Hong Kong. It was reported that the leak has killed or poisoned around 1.9 million kg of fish in the Ting River and contaminated drinking water for 60,000 people.  The government has ordered Zijin Mining Group Co Ltd to restrict gold production. Zijinshan produced 12,800t of EW copper cathode in 2009. 

- On 8<sup>th</sup> July, **Vale** announced that new five-year collective bargaining agreements have been ratified with United Steelworkers (USW) Locals 6500 and 6200 representing production and maintenance employees in **Sudbury** and Port Colborne.  The settlements mark the end of a strike that began on 13<sup>th</sup> July 2009. Employees in Ontario are expected to return to work within the next four to six weeks.  However, the strike at Vale‟s **Voisey’s Bay** operations continues. In Q1 2010, Sudbury produced 3,000t of copper-in-nickel concentrate compared with 25,000t in Q1 2009.  We have estimated production for 2010 at 52,000t copper-in-nickel concentrate, higher than 2009 production of 41,000t. 

- Also on 8<sup>th</sup> July, Chile's Congress rejected a government proposal to revamp mining royalties to help pay for reconstruction after the massive earthquake on 26<sup>th</sup> February.  The proposed change in mining royalties aimed to raise up to US$1B out of a wider US$8.4B package to fund rebuilding after the disaster by applying a variable rate from 4.0% to 9.0% of the operating margin depending on the margin‟s value.  This new royalty scheme was to be in place for two years before returning to the old scheme (flat tax rate of 4% until 2018).  If this had been accepted, then the flat tax would have been extended for a further 8 years up to 2025. 

- **Grupo Mexico** has announced plans to combine its US-based **Asarco** with its Latin American **Southern Copper** operation.  The aim is to gain cost reductions in operations and transportation, and provide synergies between the two companies.  Asarco operates three copper mines and a smelter and refinery, and Southern Copper operates the **Cananea** , **La Caridad** , **Cuajone** , **Toquepala** mines and the **San Luis Potosi** smelter.  Copper mine production at Asarco in 2009 was 181,000 tonnes and is expected to increase slightly to 190,000 tonnes this year. 

- On 15<sup>th</sup> July, it was reported that **Codelco** had reached agreements on new labour contracts with workers from unions six and two at the **Salvador** division.  In addition to a 3% wage increase, workers will receive a total bonus of 7.5M pesos (US$14,158).  These new contracts will expire in August 2013.  The life of the division has recently been extended from 2011, when production was scheduled to cease, to 2021.  The development of the US$238M **San Antonio** project will extend operations until 2038.  Construction is expected to commence in H1 2013 for sta

rt-up in 2015.

- On 16<sup>th</sup> July, it was announced that **OZ Minerals** had approved the **Prominent Hill** underground mine project.  Mining of the decline is scheduled to commence in October, with first ore accessed in Q4 2011 and full production from H2 2012.  The underground mine is expected to add 25,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate and 12,000oz/y of gold to existing open pit production.  The sub-level open stoping mining method will be used to produce 1.2Mt/y of ore.  The mine life will be 5 years.  Preproduction capital expenditure is estimated at AUD$135M (US$121M).  In 2010, output from the Prominent Hill open pit is expected to be around 110,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

## **Exploration and Development** 









- **Vale** plans to invest US$400M in Zambia's **Konkola North** copper project, and expects to start producing copper by 2013.  The Konkola North project, Vale's joint-venture project with **African Rainbow Minerals** is the first of a number of projects Vale plans to develop in Africa.  The capital required will be invested over two and half years.  Initial production will be 50,000t/y of copper rising to 100,000t/y by 2015 in Phase 2.  However, on 28<sup>th</sup> July the Mine Workers Union of Zambia announced its intention to block the development, citing concerns over Vale‟s relations with workers unions in Canada (see Production section above). 

- A rift has developed between **Rio Tinto** and **Ivanhoe Mines Ltd** , the development partners for the **Oyu Tolgoi** copper-gold project in Mongolia.  Rio Tinto has instigated arbitration over a decision by Ivanhoe‟s board in April to introduce a shareholder rights plan which Rio Tinto claims could substantially reduce the latter‟s shareholding.  Rio Tinto claims that the shareholder rights plan breaches its 2006 contract with Ivanhoe.  The plan restricts Rio Tinto‟s ability to buy shares in Ivanhoe and protect its stake (currently at 29.6% but with warrants to increase it to 44%) in the event of dilutive share issuances by Ivanhoe.  Ivanhoe Mines owns 66% of Oyu Tolgoi and the Mongolian government owns the balance.  The project is expected to come onstream in 2013 and produce around 436,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate at full production. 

- On 7<sup>th</sup> July, **Xstrata Copper** announced the approval of US$1.47B investment to develop the **Antapaccay** project.  The project is an expansion of the **Tintaya** mine and will increase Tintaya‟s copper production by 60% to an average of 160,000t/y for the first six years of the 20-year life of the Antapaccay mine.  In 2010, we expect Tintaya to produce 70,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 36,000t of EW copper cathode. 

- On 15<sup>th</sup> July, the Peruvian government announced the formal creation of a technical committee to evaluate the Environmental Impact Study (EIS) for **Southern Copper Co

rporation's** (SCC‟s) US$934M **Tia Maria** project.  This follows protests by local residents who are concerned about the project's potential environmental impact, in particular its use of water. The group will evaluate Tia Maria's EIS, after which a final report will be presented to the Mines and Energy Ministry (MEM). Tia Maria is expected to produce 120,000t/y of EW copper cathodes. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 



- **Aurubis’ Hamburg** smelter-refinery complex resumed normal production on 22<sup>nd</sup> July following a fire which halted production on 16<sup>th</sup> July. The company says that around 2,000-2,500 tonnes of copper output will be lost.  Part of the molten copper in one of the two anode furnaces leaked out and the 1,200 ºC hot melt caused cable to ignite under the anode furnace.  No one was injured during the incident and the environment was not affected.  The building was not damaged in any way.

Hamburg produced 374,000 tonnes in 2009 and is estimated to produce 380,000 tonnes in 2010.  The property damage is not expected to exceed €150,000 (US$194,000) and is limited to the anode furnace drive. 



- **Urals Mining and Metals Co (UMMC),** Russia's second largest copper producer, announced on 15<sup>th</sup> July that it plans to finish building its second refinery in Q4 2011.  Last year, UMMC said it had decided to postpone until 2012-2014 from 2010 its plan to build the refinery, which would increase the firm's capacity by 37% to 500,000 tonnes per year.  UMMC plans to raise cathode copper output in 2010 by 20% from 2009 to 370,000 tonnes, in line with its earlier target of 356,918 tonnes. 

## **Consumption** 





- Cablemaker **Nexans** has released its second quarter results.  After an 11.1% y-o-y decline in sales (at constant metal prices) in Q1, sales for Q2 rose 12.0% y-o-y as the company saw a sequential improvement across all its business lines.  Energy cables growth continued in the Middle East, Russia, Africa and France and the company will shortly open its first cable plant in Qatar.  However, due to the delay of some projects in Western Europe and Brazil, Nexans has taken the decision to close its **Latina** , Italy, energy cables plant and its **Lorena** , Brazil, aluminium overhead conductors plant.  The group expects that its sales growth will be stronger in H2 2010 than it has been in H1 2010. 

- In the Gulf States there are strong indications that the region‟s first copper tube mill may shortly be commissioned.  There has been strong interest from the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar in establishing a mid-sized mill to replace dependence on imports from overseas.  Additional wirerod capacity will also come on stream this year in the UAE and Saudi Arabia, based on committed projects.  The big unknown is over Saudi Arabia‟s **Tasnee** ‟s plans to build a combined US$1bn copper, lead and zinc s

melter at **Yanbu** in the Kingdom, and possibly with a downstream copper fabricating facility alongside it.  However, the contract for the smelter is not due to be awarded until Q3 2011 with completion due in late-2013.
